title: How the browser is built and looks

entities.title: One HTML file, no build
entities.summary: The page is a single file that runs in the reader's browser; the Worker serves it as it is.
entities.context: The browser has to be easy to host, copy and trust with a private repository.
entities.decision: Markup, styles, script and icons are in index.html. It talks to the repository's host straight from the browser, and loads only dagre, the typefaces and, on first entry to Cyberspace, three.js from jsDelivr. The Worker at cyberspace-explorer.com imports the file as text and serves it unchanged; it adds GitHub sign-in, and nothing the page needs to work.
entities.rationale: There is nothing to build, any static host can serve it, and a reader who doesn't sign in gives no server their repository or token.
entities.details: Earlier the decision was "no server" too. The Worker, with its sign-in, came later ([its decisions](worker/.dev/decisions.json)); served as a plain file the page still works, with pasted tokens.

entities.title: The page draws its own diagrams
entities.summary: dagre places parts; the page draws everything.
entities.context: Each kind of diagram reads best with its own shapes, and a general diagramming library would set the look.
entities.decision: dagre 3.1.3 only positions parts and routes lines. Shapes, lines, arrowheads, labels and icons are SVG written by the page, one drawing per kind, sharing one layout and one renderer.
entities.rationale: The drawings look like one family and like the rest of the page, and only one library is needed.

entities.title: A survey sheet: cool paper and slate ink
entities.summary: The page's look is a surveyor's sheet.
entities.context: The page is read for long stretches and is mostly drawings and tables.
entities.decision: Light: paper #edf1f1, sheet #f8fafa, plates #ffffff, ink #1d2b33 with #56666e and #84949b for secondary and faint text, rules #c9d3d5. Dark: paper #10181d, sheet #152128, plates #1b2a32, ink #dce5e5. Drawings sit on the sheet with a small cross at every 24-unit grid point, and parts are white plates with a soft shadow in their kind's colour.
entities.rationale: Quiet surfaces let the one colour per kind carry the meaning.

entities.title: One colour per kind
entities.summary: Each kind of view has one colour, used everywhere that kind appears.
entities.context: A reader moves between ten kinds of view and needs to know at a glance which one they are in.
entities.decision: Component #2c6e8e, deployment #a26a14, class #527a31, state #8b4a8c, use case #bb5430, capability #4f58b0, feature #b0456f, operation #5b6a72, user journey #1f7f74, knowledge #7a5f36, each with a lighter value for dark mode. The colour marks the kind's icon, pips, tab underline, plate outlines and tints, card edges and the inspector.
entities.rationale: The kind is recognisable from any part of the page without reading.

entities.title: Barlow in three widths
entities.summary: One type family, in three widths, with a system monospace.
entities.context: The page sets long names in narrow places: tree rows, plates, tabs, table headers.
entities.decision: Barlow (400, 500) for reading text at 16 px; Barlow Semi Condensed (500, 600) for labels, tabs, headings, the tree and inside drawings; Barlow Condensed (600, 700) for the brand, the landing headline and a folder's name, set large. Paths, IDs and symbols are in the system monospace.
entities.rationale: Condensed widths fit more of a name in a plate or a row while staying one family.

entities.title: Icons drawn for the page
entities.summary: Every icon is drawn for this page on a 24-unit grid.
entities.context: Icons mark kinds, groups and parts, and a part's icon should say what it is.
entities.decision: Strokes of 1.6 with round ends, and one tinted shape per glyph so each reads as a small solid object. A component's icon is chosen from its name (an engine gets a gear, a renderer a screen, a database a cylinder, and so on, with a cube when nothing matches); a deployment node's from its kind; a type's from its kind.
entities.rationale: The drawings say something before they are read, and the icons match the drawings.

entities.title: A folder shows one kind at a time
entities.summary: Tabs by kind, with all knowledge under one tab.
entities.context: A folder can have a dozen views and knowledge files, and drawings need room.
entities.decision: A tab per kind, in a fixed order; the open kind stays open from folder to folder. Every knowledge file shares one tab, grouped as the catalogue groups them.
entities.rationale: A reader sees one kind at full width, and following one kind through the tree keeps them on it.

entities.title: Every view is also tables
entities.summary: A drawing is a way in, not the only way.
entities.context: A drawing can fail to load, be too dense, or hide a detail.
entities.decision: Under each drawing a disclosure holds the view in full as tables: parts, relationships or transitions, related views and sources, with the file itself linked.
entities.rationale: Nothing a view says is only in a picture.

entities.title: One moment of motion
entities.summary: Opening a folder through a drawing is the page's one animation.
entities.context: Motion should say something.
entities.decision: The badged part grows into the page as its folder opens. Beyond that the page only pulses a part or flashes a record it has moved to, fades what is not lit and ticks while loading; all of it is off with reduced motion.
entities.rationale: The one movement explains where the reader has gone: into the part.

entities.title: In Cyberspace, motion takes the reader where they asked
entities.summary: Cyberspace's camera moves are motion beyond one-motion: they only take the reader where they asked to go, and reduced motion turns them all off.
entities.context: Decision one-motion allows the page one animation, the drill. Cyberspace needs camera moves: flying to a part, sliding a floor out of the folder tower, rising from the street back to the city.
entities.decision: In Cyberspace, motion only moves the camera, or a floor, to where the reader asked to go: flights between poses, a floor sliding out and back, and the fades that go with a change of scene. Nothing moves on its own. With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce every flight, slide and fade is instant; walking still moves, because the reader drives it. This amends one-motion; Flat keeps its one moment of motion.
entities.rationale: A move the reader asked for shows where they went, as the drill does in Flat; motion nobody asked for would only distract.
entities.details: Cyberspace has no motion yet: its camera stands still until the camera rig is built (plan cyberspace-mode, step city).

entities.title: The address is the state
entities.summary: Once a repository is open, the address says what is shown.
entities.context: Links are how readers share what they see.
entities.decision: The repository is in ?url= and the place in it after #. The landing page's form only sets ?url=; there is no address field once a repository is open, and Choose another repository returns to the landing page.
entities.rationale: Every place can be linked to, and back and forward work.

entities.title: Tokens stay in the reader's browser, by scope
entities.summary: Each token is kept under the host and scope it is for.
entities.context: Readers have private repositories on several hosts and accounts, and must not leak a token to the wrong host.
entities.decision: Tokens are kept in sessionStorage, or localStorage when asked, under a scope; the narrowest scope around a repository wins. GitHub files are read from raw.githubusercontent.com without a token and through the API with one, because raw.githubusercontent.com turns away an Authorization header.
entities.rationale: No server holds a pasted token, and several accounts work side by side.
entities.details: A reader signed in with GitHub through the Worker uses that sign-in for GitHub instead, and the Worker holds that token ([token-off-the-page](worker/.dev/decisions.json)).

entities.title: A repository may keep all its views in .cyberspace-explorer
entities.summary: A .cyberspace-explorer folder at the root can hold what the .dev folders would, folder by folder.
entities.context: A .dev folder in every folder spreads views through the source tree, which some repositories would rather keep out of it.
entities.decision: foo/.dev/x.json and .cyberspace-explorer/foo/x.json mean the same, and .cyberspace-explorer/x.json is the root folder's x.json. If the root has a .cyberspace-explorer folder the page reads only that and does not look for .dev folders. A path written either way in a view finds the same view.
entities.rationale: One folder at the root holds every view, and a repository that has not moved is read as before.

entities.title: Cyberspace appears when it is whole
entities.summary: Each step of Cyberspace is merged and deployed as it is built, but the Flat / Cyberspace switch appears only when step 7 is done.
entities.context: Merging to main deploys to cyberspace-explorer.com, and the Worker has no preview URLs. Cyberspace is built in eight pull requests (plan cyberspace-mode).

options.title: Merge every step, the switch hidden until step 7
options.consequences: Small changes that never drift from main, and nothing half-built for readers. The changes to route() and select() reach readers before the launch, so every step checks the flat page again.

options.title: Merge every step, the switch shown from step 1
options.consequences: Readers find a mode that at first shows only a grid, and that lacks keyboard, reduced-motion and light-mode support until step 7.

options.title: One long-lived branch, merged once
options.consequences: Nothing reaches readers early, but the branch drifts while others change index.html, and one large merge is hard to review.

entities.decision: One pull request per step into main. The switch is built in step 1 and stays hidden until step 7 meets the recorded quality requirements: keyboard, reduced motion, light and dark, fallbacks. Until then only an address with ~space in it opens Cyberspace.
entities.rationale: Changes stay small enough to review, and readers see Cyberspace only when it is whole.

entities.title: Cyberspace: a second way in, in 3D
entities.summary: Beside Flat, the same .dev files can be read as a WebGL scene laid out on the flat drawing's ground plan, drawn with three.js core and the page's own controls and labels.
entities.context: Flat shows a folder's views as drawings, cards and tables. The design canvas Cyberspace explorer in 3D (copied in docs/cyberspace-design/) shows the same views as a tower of floors, a city of glass towers and a street to walk.
entities.decision: Cyberspace is a second way into the same data, never the only one: everything it shows stays readable in Flat, which shows instead wherever Cyberspace can't run. Its ground plan is the flat layout: a part stands where dagre puts its plate on the flat sheet. It is drawn with three.js core only (no OrbitControls, CSS2DRenderer or any other addon, and no post-processing); the camera controls and the labels are the page's own. three.js is pinned to one version and imported from jsDelivr on first entry, as dagre is. An address whose last segment is ~space opens it.
entities.rationale: A reader who switches modes finds everything in the same place. Core three.js is the one new download, and controls and labels written for the page look like the page.
entities.details: Built so far: the address, the switch (hidden until the launch), the fallbacks, and a scene of sky and ground grid. The city, laid out on the flat layout, comes with the plan's next step.

entities.title: The Cyberspace design is copied into the repository
entities.summary: docs/cyberspace-design/ holds the canvas's three artboards and a render of each; the canvas stays the source.
entities.context: The design is a private claude.ai canvas. The agents who build Cyberspace, and anyone reviewing it, can't open it, so the spec's "match the artboard" couldn't be checked.
entities.decision: The three artboards (static HTML) and a 1440 × 900 render of each are copied into docs/cyberspace-design/, with a README that says what they show and what they don't. The design changes on the canvas and is copied here again.
entities.rationale: The design can be seen wherever the repository can.

entities.title: What a repository with several folders looks like in Cyberspace
entities.summary: The canvas has one folder only. The skyline that shows several has a layout rule in the spec, but no design.
entities.context: In Cyberspace a folder is a tower of floors. With several folders, the spec lays them out as buildings on a radial tree from the root, each as tall as it has views, with dashed ground lines from parent to child; clicking one flies into it. No artboard shows this, and most repositories have several folders.

options.title: An artboard on the canvas first
options.consequences: Step 6 builds to a design, and the skyline's polish waits for it.

options.title: Build the spec's rule, design it afterwards
options.consequences: Nothing waits; the look may change later.

entities.title: Cyberspace in light mode
entities.summary: The canvas is dark only. The spec derives light mode from the page's tokens, and nobody has seen it.
entities.context: Every colour in Cyberspace comes from the page's tokens (quality requirement light-dark), with four new ones for the sky and the major grid, so light mode follows from the light values. The canvas has no light artboard.

options.title: One light artboard per scene before step 7
options.consequences: Light mode is designed, not derived; step 7 waits for three artboards.

options.title: Take what the tokens give, and review it in step 7
options.consequences: Nothing waits; light mode may need a pass after the launch.

entities.title: How state machines, use cases and parts that open a folder stand in Cyberspace
entities.summary: The canvas has only a component city. The spec gives defaults for what it doesn't show.
entities.context: Cyberspace draws every drawn kind as a city, but the canvas shows a component diagram only. The spec's defaults: a state machine's start point is a disc on the ground; a final state has a second band; a use case's alternative outcome is a short tower with dashed edges, not a beacon (a beacon is outside the browser); a part with diagrams of its own carries the drill icon and offers Enter its folder.

options.title: Add a state-machine city and a use-case city to the canvas
options.consequences: The defaults change where the artboards say otherwise.

entities.title: Use cases and journeys side by side in Cyberspace
entities.summary: A file of several use cases becomes one city per use case. Whether readers can stand them side by side is decided after step 6.
entities.context: Flat draws one canvas per use case or journey, and the spec builds one city per entity, chosen in the address. Standing several side by side would be the Layers mechanism of step 6 applied to entities.

entities.title: Who checks Cyberspace in Safari and Firefox
entities.summary: The acceptance checklist runs in Chrome, Safari and Firefox, and only Chrome can be driven by an agent on the machine the work is checked on.
entities.context: That machine has Chrome for Testing, but no WebKit or Firefox build an agent can drive.

options.title: The owner runs the checklist in Safari and Firefox
options.consequences: Nothing to download; the owner's time at steps 7 and 8.

options.title: Install Playwright's WebKit and Firefox builds
options.consequences: About 200 MB downloaded once; an agent runs the checklist in all three.
